analysis.title: Not quite Volmageddon... yet
key_insights: VIX, VVIX and tech volatility (VXN) are surging. VVIX shows greater stress than VIX, and VXN is approaching Liberation Day panic levels.
The short end of the VIX term structure is spiking as traders rush to buy immediate downside hedges, hurting those who took yesterday's rebound as an all-clear.
The VIX 2/8-month futures ratio is rising sharply, which TME treats as a preferred under-the-hood stress indicator and a sign of near-term risk being repriced against longer-dated volatility.

Vanda Research says the selloff and volatility spike bring CTA selling back into play. A break below 27,600 could push CTAs outright short, and a clean break below 26,800 could take CTA exposure toward Liberation Day lows.
Skew (SDEX index) remains below mid-October levels despite the volatility spike, which may mean investors are cutting delta exposure instead of buying more expensive downside protection.
Implied correlations are rising but remain far from extreme, so the market is not pricing a correlation shock.
CNN Fear & Greed Index is in extreme fear, but sentiment was more bearish in October, so this is not yet capitulation.
TME's read is a market in panic mode but not a full Volmageddon. The risk is that persistently elevated volatility triggers further deleveraging.
risk_factors: Persistently elevated volatility could trigger further deleveraging and turn the volatility shock into something much worse.
A break below 27,600 and then 26,800 could add systematic CTA selling to an already stressed market.
